after.title: Feeding mechanism
after.description: Dwarf sperm whales take squid and other prey using suction-assisted feeding. Their underslung lower jaw bears most teeth. The pale false-gill crescent is skin pigment; the animal breathes air through a blowhole and has no gills. Defensive reddish fluid is released from the intestine.
after.modelCoverage: Biological account. The closed-mouth exterior does not simulate prey capture or internal oral mechanics.

after.title: Respiration
after.description: A single dorsal blowhole admits air at the surface. Breathing is separate from feeding; submerged apnea does not use gills. The displayed slit is closed. Ventilation, oxygen stores and circulation are not computed.
after.modelCoverage: External closed blowhole anatomy only.

after.title: Locomotion and control
after.description: Dorsoventral bending of the posterior body drives horizontal flukes. Pectoral flippers assist control; they do not flap like penguin wings. The turning study combines heading change, lateral body curvature and a small bank. Timing and amplitude are uncalibrated display parameters.
after.modelCoverage: Exterior kinematics, with no solved fluid forces or speed estimate.

after.title: Skin and phenotype
after.description: Compact, deep body with a sloping blunt head, short underslung mouth, small flippers and a relatively tall central dorsal fin. The false-gill crescent follows the eye region and is only pigment. Smooth glabrous skin is rendered with subtle variable roughness; scars and individual pigment boundaries are illustrative.
after.modelCoverage: Original exterior pigment and low-relief maps, not measured tissue optics.
